answer.justification: Resistant hypertension with hypokalemia (K 3.3) and metabolic alkalosis (HCO3 33) indicates mineralocorticoid excess. Primary hyperaldosteronism causes sodium retention with potassium and hydrogen ion wasting, causing cramps, fatigue, and hypertension unresponsive to standard antihypertensives.
